lanes.summary: The diff implements exactly what PMAT-678 asks: a `make publish-from-tag TAG=` target that shells out to `scripts/publish-from-tag.sh`, which refuses (exit 2) before any cargo call when TAG is empty/malformed/nonexistent/off origin-master/version-mismatched, builds a `git worktree add --detach` checkout, verifies it is pristine (exit 3 otherwise), runs `env -u CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN cargo publish --dry-run --locked`, stops there under DRY_RUN=1, otherwise re-checks cleanliness and runs `env -u CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN cargo publish --locked`, and removes the worktree via an EXIT trap. Both belt items are present (`.claude/agent-memory/` added to `.gitignore`; `release-verify` now does `cargo install pmat --locked --force`). The accompanying audit harness (`publish-from-tag-audit.sh`) exercises 11 arms with a shim `cargo` and a self-test that is RED against a no-op script, and its logic checks out on inspection (fixture tags an off-master commit and a same-commit/mismatched-version tag correctly, the shim captures cwd git-common-dir/toplevel/status/token to catch a leaked token or a main-tree run). The one disclosed deviation — the ticket's "dropping --detach → zero-untracked-files assertion RED" falsifier is explained as untestable because `git worktree add <dir> <tag>` detaches regardless of the flag — is transparently documented in both the receipt and a "MUTATION GUARD" comment in the script, and the flag itself is still present in the implementation, so nothing required by the ticket was silently dropped. No test asserts the opposite of the ticket, no gate is weakened (the change adds --locked in two places, never removes a check), and I found no diff content outside the ticket's scope (docs/roadmap bookkeeping aside, which is standard).

lanes.summary: Diff implements PMAT-678 completely: publish-from-tag Makefile target with git worktree --detach, env -u CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, --locked flags, and cleanup trap. Belt items present: .claude/agent-memory/ in .gitignore, --locked on release-verify. Script robustly validates TAG format, existence, ancestry to origin/master, and Cargo.toml version match before creating worktree. No contradictions with ticket or receipt.
